title: Runtime protocol negotiation and Accept-Version header policy
creator: Maya Patel
description: Purpose: Define a concrete runtime semantic versioning policy that enables safe evolution of the serving runtime via explicit protocol negotiation. This ticket establishes: (1) how clients indicate acceptable runtime API versions (Accept-Version style header), (2) server-side routing and fallback behavior, (3) deprecation/notice headers and advisory windows, (4) telemetry-driven rollout gate thresholds, and (5) an automated lightweight adapter template for non-breaking to breaking translations.
acceptance_criteria: Spec document published in the release-infra RFC repo describing Accept-Version header format and precedence rules
Runtime implements header parsing and routing with deterministic fallback to a compatible minor/patch channel within 1 sprint
Server emits deprecation and upgrade advisory headers for deprecated endpoints: X-RW-Deprecated and X-RW-Deprecation-ETA
Canary rollout policy reads telemetry signals (error-rate, p50/p99 latency, request-compat-mismatch) and can abort rollouts when thresholds exceeded
An adapter template repo exists that can be used to generate shims for a limited set of breaking changes (field rename, optional->required, enum delta) and CI checks run the adapter during drafts
design_notes: We intentionally separate protocol negotiation (client tells server what versions it understands) from model runtime versioning. The Accept-Version header is scoped to the runtime API surface (inference request schema, streaming frames, tool-calling payloads). Priority rules: explicit Accept-Version takes precedence over request-level version query param; default behavior is to route to pinned customer runtime version or the latest compatible stable channel. Major version bump indicates potentially breaking changes: server will not auto-upgrade client traffic across majors without explicit opt-in. Minor version changes may introduce additive, opt-in features and backward-compatible extensions.
negotiation_format: Clients SHOULD send: Accept-Version: runtime/MAJOR.MINOR[.PATCH]; q=0.9. Wildcards allowed: runtime/* or runtime/MAJOR.*. Multiple versions MAY be listed with q-values. If no Accept-Version header is present, server will assume 'latest-stable' for hosted customers and 'pinned' for Dedicated/Private installations.
fallback_policy: Server routing: 1) exact match -> route. 2) if unavailable, try same major with highest minor <= requested minor (compatible fallback). 3) if still unavailable, consult customer pinning: if the customer has a pinned runtime, route there. 4) last resort: return 406 Not Acceptable with X-RW-Compat-Options header listing available versions and a machine-readable reason code. For requests with function/tool-calling schemas, the server may attempt to run an adapter shim only when adapter templates declare coverage for the change type.
deprecation_headers: When we deprecate fields or endpoints, servers must emit: X-RW-Deprecated: vMAJOR.MINOR (first deprecated version), X-RW-Deprecation-ETA: YYYY-MM-DD (end-of-life date), X-RW-Deprecation-Note: short human message. Deprecation window defaults: 90 days for additive changes, 180 days for removal of fields/endpoints, and 1 year for removal of top-level API compatibility points. These windows can be extended per-release with PM signoff.
telemetry_gates: Signals used by rollout automation: client-compat-mismatch-rate, request-error-rate, user-latency-p50/99, user-retry-rate, adapter-fallback-rate. Default abort thresholds for canary: client-compat-mismatch-rate > 0.5% over a 10-minute window OR request-error-rate increase > 2x baseline AND absolute p99 latency increase > 200ms. Metrics come from Console tracing and per-token cost dashboards. Alerting + automated rollback configured in the rollout orchestration job.
adapter_strategy: Provide a minimal adapter generator that outputs deterministic translation layers for supported change patterns: 1) simple field rename (old->new mapping), 2) enum expansion with fallback token, 3) deprecate optional -> required by synthesizing defaults when safe. Adapters are not a universal solution—they must be transparent and logged via X-RW-Adapter-Used header. The generator will live in infra/adapters and produce small Lua/Go transformation hooks that the runtime can load into a staging canary.
rollout_plan: Phase A: RFC review and design sign-off (1 week). Phase B: implement header parsing and simple routing + tests (2 sprints). Phase C: deprecation header emitters and documentation + console UX for version negotiation visibility (1 sprint). Phase D: adapter generator MVP + canary rollout with telemetry gates (2 sprints). Phase E: public docs and migration assistant (1 sprint). Total: ~7 sprints of cross-functional work; scope can be trimmed for runtime-1.20 MVP to only include header parsing, header emissions, and basic routing.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: over-reliance on adapters leads to hidden correctness bugs. Mitigation: adapters must be explicit opt-in per-customer and logged; require canary approval and integration tests that exercise adapter transformations against golden prompts. Risk: noisy telemetry during first rollouts. Mitigation: baseline period and synthetic traffic to establish stable baselines, progressive throttling of canaries.
tasks: Add Accept-Version parser and unit tests to runtime/http/negotiation package
Implement X-RW-Deprecated header emission in validation layers
Create adapter-generator MVP in infra/adapters and a sample shim for enum-renames
Console: add per-route 'accepted versions' visualization and request-level version header display
Rollout job: wire telemetry gates and automated rollback hooks
